objectives.a1: Find the Larkfold cart at Ferrow Cross, down the mountain road south-east of Larkfold.
objectives.a1b: Talk to the big man by the well.
objectives.a2: Go east to the Commons camp, up on the Old Drove Road. Brannoc knows the way.
objectives.a3: Stop the indenture cart at Hob's Bend, east of Millbridge.
objectives.a3c: See to the children from the cart.
objectives.a4: Take the children back to the Commons camp and report to Kane.
objectives.a5: Go to Millbridge with Lieutenant Varro. The town meets in the square.
objectives.a6: Join Kane's attack on the Sallow hatchery, south-east of Hob's Bend.
objectives.a6b: The brood house is burning. Get to its door through the yard.
objectives.a7: The first harvest since the raid. Leave the camp by the west track and go home to Larkfold.
objectives.a7c: Go back down to the others, by the south gate. The spring caves are still there.
objectives.a2b: Look round the camp: the nurses' tent, the drill yard and the kith lines. Then go back to Kane.
objectives.a2c: Night watch on the east picket, at the top of the camp. Ferris is already there.
objectives.a2d: Kane has sent for Brannoc's section.
objectives.a5b: A quiet month at the camp. Spend time with your people. Kane will send for you when there's work.
objectives.a6c: Walk back to the Commons camp. Brannoc was carried ahead to the nurses' tent, and he's asking for you.
objectives.a6d: The section meets at the fire tonight. Sit with them.
objectives.a2e: Turn in for the night. Your tent is the one in the top-left corner of the camp, by the west fence.
objectives.a2f: Dawn. Brannoc is waiting for you in the drill yard.
objectives.a2g: Three weeks of drill ahead. When you're ready, turn in at your tent.
objectives.a2h: Your watch is over. Go back to your tent and sleep.
objectives.a4b: Walk back to the Commons camp, east on the Old Drove Road, and turn in at your tent.
objectives.a6e: Go to bed, Sergeant. Your tent is in the top-left corner of the camp.

then.text: "If you're after the Larkfold cart, it's in the yard. What's left of it."

else.text: "The Guild pays me to keep that cart and say nothing. I'm saying nothing, and I'm sorry for it."

talk.text: "Eat something, Caddow. You can't fight on spite alone. I've tried."

then.text: "That little one from the cart, Sela? She's taken over the kith lines. Told me I was holding a loftbuck wrong."

else.text: "Half of us were miners. The other half were hatchery children once. Nobody here wears a lull. Not one."

then.text: "The children from the cart are sleeping. First night in a year without a bell, one of them said."

else.text: "Every child we take out of a hatchery comes here first. We've room for more. We always have room for more."

talk.text: "Don't laugh. She's my reedcat. She's just decided I'm prey today. If you know any way to calm a kith, I'm listening."
A reedcat, hackles up, tail lashing at the foot of the tree. Ferris is up in the branches. A song might settle her.
A boy of about ten. He won't let go of the cart's wheel, and he won't say his name. Only his number.

then.text: "I'll talk to you when the reeve's heard you. Not before."

else.text: "Go on, then. You've said your piece."

talk.text: "My brother wore a Larkfold greenling for two months. He was getting better. Then he didn't wake up."
A man at the stall sells lull tins with the Guild's stamp. He doesn't look at Rhea.
"Kane says the Sallow hatchery. Tonight. You're to take the gate. South-east of Hob's Bend, you can't miss the chimneys."
"Two at the gate. Take them, Caddow, and the yard's ours. Don't wait for me."
"The reeve is ringing the bell for us. Talk to her when you're ready, Caddow."

then.text: "Go on. Kane's been looking for you."

talk.text: "I'm only here to listen. Nurse's orders: no voting, no laughing."

do.toast: Hob's Bend. An empty road through the trees.
The Sallow hatchery. Wardens on the wall, and smoke from the brood house chimneys. Not with three people.
Vantry, the Guild's city. Finch is somewhere behind those walls. Not yet.
A ruined monastery on a terrace over a hot spring. Thornwick. Nobody has lived here for a hundred years.
The Cloudline terraces. The clans watch you pass and say nothing. Another year, perhaps.
Not yet. Not until the harvest.
A shut door. Someone inside is coughing.
A shut door. A child's face at the window, then gone.
The heat from the door is too much.
You came up to sing. Sing first.

do.text: The Larkfold cart. Someone has scratched a little horned loftbuck into the tailboard, low down, where a child sitting on the floor could reach.
The cart is empty now. The children are sitting in the grass, sharing Brannoc's bread.
The water tastes of iron.
Bedrolls, a pot, a pair of boots drying. Somebody has pinned a child's drawing of a loftbuck to the canvas.
Bread, onions, a tray of lull tins with the Guild's stamp. The tins sell out first.
Eleven names are chalked on the well's stones. The rain has nearly washed them off.
You sing it once more, quietly. The cloud goes on moving below the terraces.

fail.text: The heat drives you back to the gate.

act1Start.text: "Another road, Rhea. That's ten since the carts took Finch. We've worn out two pairs of boots each."
"A carter swore he saw the Larkfold cart at Ferrow Cross. The coaching inn, at the bottom of the mountain road."
"Same as the last ten times, then. If it's not there, we eat, we sleep, and we try the next road."

emptyCart.text: The Larkfold cart is standing in the yard with its tailboard down. It's empty.
There's straw on the floor, a child's mitten, and a little loftbuck scratched into the wood, low down. Finch drew Smoke like that on every wall in Larkfold.

"They split the children here, last autumn. Some to the Guild's houses in Vantry, some to the outer hatcheries, some down the river. A Warden stood by the stove and fed the cart's ledger into it, page by page."
"Where did the boy go? Twelve years old then, sandy hair. He'd have been holding on to a lead rope. He'd have been asking about a loftbuck."
"I'm sorry. There were forty of them. I didn't look at their faces. I made myself not look."
Rhea sits down on the tailboard. Tamsin sits beside her and doesn't say anything, which is the kindest thing anyone has done in a year.
"Rhea. The man by the well has been watching us since we came in."

meetBrannoc.text: "I'm sorry about the cart. I've seen a lot of empty ones."
He's huge, and gentle with it, the way some very big men learn to be. His neck is a ladder of old pale rings. Eleven of them.
"Brannoc. Sergeant, Commons Army. Miners, farmers, kids we've pulled out of hatcheries. Anyone the Guild has had its hands on. I came down for the same cart. We heard about it too late as well."
"You won't find him on the roads. The Guild's records are burned and its hatcheries have walls. One woman with a staff can't open a hatchery. An army can."
"Every child we pull out of a hatchery goes in a book at our camp. Name, village, the cart they came on. Some of the names we've had off Guild clerks."

do.text: "I didn't ask you to. I asked you to come and read a book."
"You shouldn't. Trust what it does. Come and see the camp, and the children in it, and then decide."

"Eleven months, after a roof came down on me in the Kerrow mines. One ring for every lull. Getting off them took longer than wearing them. I've been clean six years. Some days I'm proud of it, some days it's just a long time."

meetBrannoc.text: "I'll read your book. Then I'm back on the road."
"I'll come too. Somebody has to make sure you eat."
"Our camp's up on the Old Drove Road, east of the river. I'll walk with you."

then.text: "You're on the east picket tonight, Caddow. Ferris is already there."
"Millbridge, Caddow. Varro will do the talking. You tell them the truth about Larkfold, whatever it costs."

else.text: "Nothing for you this week. Rest while you can, Caddow. Tamsin was asking after you."
"Every hatchery we open is a few hundred children and one less wall between you and your brother. Keep going, Caddow."

enlist.text: Marshal Idris Kane is younger than Rhea expected, with an easy smile and a green coat gone grey at the seams. He listens like he has all day.
"Brannoc says you've walked every cart road in the highlands for a year. He says you want to read our book."
The book is three fingers thick. Rhea reads every page from the spring of the raid onwards, and then reads them again. Finch isn't in it.
"Not yet. Every hatchery we open adds pages."

options.label: "The Guild took my brother. I want him back."

do.text: "Then we want the same thing, near enough. Every hatchery we open is a door he might be behind."

options.label: "I want every hatchery in Ostrel burned."

do.text: "Burned's easy. Opened is harder. The children inside need the doors open, not the roofs on fire. Remember that, and you'll do well here."

options.label: "My husband led the Wardens into my village."

do.text: "Ah. Then you know better than anyone what the Guild does to the people it owns. I'm sorry, Caddow."

enlist.text: "I came to read a book, Marshal. I've read it."

"Then stay one night before you go. Brannoc tells me you're a doctor, and my nurses are stitching scalps with sailmaker's thread. Have a look round: the nurses' tent, the drill yard, the kith lines. Then come and tell me what you saw."

ferrisDown.text: Rhea sings the foal song, low and slow. The reedcat's ears turn towards her. Its tail stops lashing. It sits.
Then it yawns, very wide, and walks off to wash itself as if nothing had happened.
"She's never done that for anyone. Not even me."
He climbs down, scratched and red-faced, and the reedcat comes back to wind round his legs.
"Ferris. I scout for Kane, when she lets me. This is Thistle. If you ever need someone to go ahead of you quietly, we'll both come."

cartFight.text: "Stand aside. This cart carries indentured property of the Brood Guild."
He's alone, as Kane promised, and he doesn't look afraid. The others hang back. This one is Rhea's.

win.text: The cart warden goes down in the road and stays down. Rhea stands over him, breathing hard, with her staff still raised.
"He's done, Caddow. Leave him for the Wardens to find. The children first."

openCart.text: Rhea opens the tailboard. Eight children look out at her from the straw. None of them makes a sound. They've learned not to.
Finch isn't one of them. She knew he wouldn't be, and it still takes her breath.
"You're safe. We're taking you somewhere warm. Nobody's going to put you in a hatchery."

then.text: The smallest of them, a girl of about eight with a number stitched on her collar, climbs down first. She's from Larkfold. Rhea knows her face.

selaFree.text: "Sela? Sela, it's Rhea. From the terraces."

"They took me with Finch. Then a Warden paid for me. He went into the hut with the captain and came out and said my name, and they put me in a different cart, to the sorting house, not the brood rooms. I never saw his face. He had his back to the lamp."
"Then last week a clerk said the sorting house was full, and put me in this one."
"I don't know. Nobody pays for us."
Rhea holds her for a long time.

selaFree.toast: Sela is safe. She'll go to the Commons camp.

afterCart.text: "Eight children out of a Guild cart and not a scratch on them. Brannoc says you held your nerve, Caddow. Good."
"Now something harder. Millbridge. They buried eleven people last year, all wearing Larkfold greenlings, and they think the highlands poisoned them on purpose."
"Without Millbridge's bridge and its market we can't feed this army through the winter. Lieutenant Varro is going to speak to their town meeting."
"She wants a witness from Larkfold. Someone who was there when it burned. That's you, if you'll do it."

else.text: "Millbridge has made its choice. I hope it was the right one."

townMeeting.text: A grey-haired woman rings the market bell, and the square fills. Lieutenant Varro of the Commons stands on the well steps in a green coat, and the crowd looks at her and then, mostly, at Rhea.
"I'm Aske, reeve of this town, which means these people voted me in and can vote me out. Say your piece, Lieutenant. They'll decide."

"Millbridge. The Guild sells you a lull for a month and raises the price every time. It owns the shop, the cart, the hatchery and the bridge toll. The Commons asks for none of that. We ask for your bridge to stay open to us, and your market on the first of the month."
"I've brought someone who can tell you what the Guild does to a village that stops buying. Caddow?"
Rhea tells them about Larkfold: the Wardens on the cloud path, the drying house going up, the children in the carts. The square is quiet while she talks.
"Eleven of ours died in their sleep last harvest, Caddow. Every one of them wore a Larkfold greenling. My own sister. Tell us why."
A broad man in a stonemason's apron pushes to the front of the crowd. His hands are white with stone dust.
"My Anna was one of them. Thirty-one years married. She was getting better."
Rhea knows what the elders said: that Guild agents tampered with the brood. She believed it. She still wants to.

townMeeting.choose: What does Rhea tell Millbridge about the brood?

options.label: Tell them the truth: they all wore Larkfold's greenlings, and she doesn't know why.

do.text: "They all wore our greenlings. I don't know why that brood was too strong. The elders said the Guild did it, and I wanted to believe them, but nobody ever proved it. I'm sorry. I'm so sorry."
Nobody cheers. A few people walk away. But Oren Tull, the stonemason, comes and stands next to her, facing the crowd.
"My wife died wearing one of your greenlings, Caddow. And you've stood up there in front of all of us and said so, when you could have blamed the Guild and been cheered for it."
"The Guild has never once told us the truth about anything it sold us. I'll hear what the Commons has to offer."
One by one, a few others come and stand beside him. Not many. Enough to keep the meeting going.

do.toast: Some of Millbridge stays to listen. Some goes home angry.

options.hint: The truth, as far as she knows it.

options.label: Repeat the elders' story: Guild agents tampered with the brood.

do.text: "The Guild did this. Their agents got into our caves and fouled the brood, so you'd go back to their lulls. It's what they do."
The square roars. It's what they want to hear: someone to blame who isn't dead. By evening Millbridge has voted to open its bridge to the Commons.
Oren Tull doesn't vote. He goes home before the end, and Rhea sees him look back once from his door.

do.toast: Millbridge joins the Commons at once.

options.hint: What the elders told her. What the square wants to hear.

townMeeting.text: "Thank you, Caddow. Whatever they decide, that took nerve."
"We start back for the camp tonight. Get some rest when we're there. The rains are coming, and it'll be quiet for a while."

win.text: The gate swings open. Across the yard the brood house is already burning: a boiler has gone, or someone has fired it to cover the Wardens' retreat.
"The children are still inside. Go, Caddow!"

ketti.text: Before Rhea reaches the door, it opens from inside.
A girl of about twelve walks out of the smoke with a small child on her hip and another by the hand. Her hair is singed. There's a fresh burn along her jaw. She doesn't stop walking.
"Here, love, give them to me. We'll look after them."
"No. They're mine. I've had them since the bell. Nobody takes them."
"There's more in there. Back corner, under the trays. I couldn't carry them all."

Brannoc and Tamsin go in with wet cloths over their faces and come out with four more. Brannoc goes back for the last two alone. He comes out with both children and the brood-house roof comes down behind him, across his back. Nobody dies in the Sallow hatchery tonight. Brannoc very nearly does.

ketti.choose: The girl stands there with the two children, daring anyone to try.

options.label: Let her keep them.

do.text: "Then you'd better come with us, all three of you. What's your name?"
"Ketti. I know how to use a knife. They made us cut the brood sacks."

options.hint: She stays with them, and with you.

options.label: Hand the little ones to the army nurses.

do.text: "They need a doctor, and so do you. The nurses won't split you up. I promise."
The girl lets the nurse take them, one finger at a time. Then she walks off into the dark and doesn't come back.

options.hint: The children are safer. She may not forgive it.

ketti.text: By dawn the Sallow hatchery is ash, and two hundred and six children are sitting in the road wrapped in Commons blankets.
The nurses lift Brannoc onto a stretcher and carry him ahead, up the road to the camp. He doesn't let go of Rhea's sleeve until they make him.

harvest.text: The terraces have gone back to weeds. The houses are black shells. The drying house is a black frame against the cloud.
Every harvest of her life, this valley was full of people singing. The foal song carried from terrace to terrace, and the young loftbucks came down out of the cloud to it.

harvestSong.text: Rhea stands on the top terrace, where Finch used to stand, and sings the foal song out across the burned terraces.
She sings it all the way through. Then she sings it again.
The cloud moves below the valley. Nothing comes. Nothing comes.
She takes Corran's ring out from under her shirt, on its cord, and holds it until it's warm. She doesn't throw it away. She hates herself a little for that.

oda.text: "Rhea? Rhea Caddow? I heard singing. I thought I'd finally gone mad."
Old Oda, who kept the greenling trays. She's thin as a stick, and there's moss under her nails. She has lived in the spring caves since the raid.
"I hid in the warm pool when the Wardens came. After, I couldn't leave. Somebody had to keep the trays alive. Somebody had to know the strengths, in case."
"I've kept three trays going. Weak ones, the first strengths, for weaning. Is there anyone left to wean?"
"There's an army of them, Oda. Come down with me."

oda.toast: Oda comes down the mountain with you, carrying her trays.

leaveLarkfold.text: At the south gate Rhea stops and looks back. Then she goes down to the others.
At the bottom of the mountain road, Brannoc is waiting with the others, his back still stiff, leaning on a spear like a walking stick.
"Harvest's in. So's resting. Where are we going, Sergeant?"

tourNurse.text: The nurses' tent smells of boiled cloth and lye. A woman with her sleeves rolled up is stitching a boy's scalp by lamplight, and doing it badly.
"Brannoc said you were the doctor at Larkfold. Is that true, or is it one of his stories?"

tourNurse.choose: The boy flinches at every stitch.

do.text: You wash your hands, take the needle, and close the cut in six small stitches while the boy is still deciding whether to cry.
"Well. You can come back any time you like."
"Liar. But thank you."

tourNurse.text: "Most of what we see isn't wounds. It's the raw. Half this camp came off Guild lulls to get here, and it takes a year to stop shaking."

tourYard.text: In the drill yard a dozen people are practising with spears made of broom handles. Half of them are older than Rhea. A few are younger than Finch.
"You're the doctor Brannoc walked up? If you stay, pray you get his section. He makes you run up the drove road with a sack of stones, and then he carries your sack back down."
"There's no Guild pay here, and no lulls. You get fed, you get a blanket, and you get a vote in your section. That's the Commons."

tourKith.text: The kith lines are a row of pens made from hurdles and rope. A dozen loftbucks, two old ironbacks, and a single reedcat up a tree with a man above her in the branches.

else.text: "You haven't seen the kith lines yet. Go and look. Ferris will be up a tree."
"Go and see the drill yard first. That's where you'll live for a while."
"See the nurses' tent first. Brannoc tells me you're a doctor. They'll want to meet you."

options.label: "An army that's mostly children and people in the raw."

do.text: "Yes. That's what the Guild leaves behind, and that's what we're made of. They fight harder than you'd think."
"Every one. Nobody's indentured here. Remember that when you're tired of them."

firstWeek.text: "So. The road in the morning, or here?"

options.label: "Armies take children too. I saw your drill yard."

do.text: "So did I, the first time. Nobody under fifteen here carries more than a broom handle, and every one of them can walk out of that gate tonight. The children in a hatchery can't."

options.label: "I came for Finch, not for your war."

do.text: "Then use us. One woman can't open a hatchery. When we open the one he's in, you'll want to be first through the door, and you won't be, unless you're with us."
"A year of your life, most likely. No pay. A vote in your section, which you'll get sick of. And orders from Brannoc, which is the hard part."

firstWeek.text: Outside the tent flap, a boy from the nurses' tent has fallen asleep against a pole, with a pale new ring on his neck. He can't be much older than Finch. Nobody here is making him stay.
"One year, Marshal. If Finch turns up in your book, I go to him, whatever my orders say."
"If he turns up in my book, I'll lend you the cart."

firstWeek.toast: You enlist in the Commons Army as a Recruit.

firstWeek.text: "You'll be in Brannoc's section. Eight of them, nine with you. They'll teach you more than I can."
"Get some sleep. Your tent's the one in the top corner, by the west fence. Brannoc wants to see what you can do with that staff, at dawn. Don't let him be gentle with you."

nightWatch.text: Ferris has a blanket round his shoulders and a pot of something hot that he swears is tea. Down the slope, the Old Drove Road is a pale stripe in the dark.
"First watch? Don't stare at one place. Your eyes start making things up. Look past things, not at them."
"I drove for the Guild, you know. Four years. Carts of Guild lulls down to Millbridge, carts of children back. They pay the drivers by the trip, so you don't ask what's under the canvas."

nightWatch.choose: Ferris drinks his tea and doesn't look at you.

do.text: "One of them knocked on the boards from inside. All the way from Hob's Bend to Sallow. Same three knocks, every mile. I thought, someone's taught her that. Someone's told her to keep knocking so they know she's alive."
"I let her out at the ford and drove the empty cart into the river. Then I walked here."
"Every one. They go through Hob's Bend on the full moon, because the warden's paid extra for night driving and the Guild likes to save money on lamps."

nightWatch.text: Something moves on the road below: a shape low to the ground, then gone. Ferris lifts a hand before you can stand.
"Fox kith. If it were Wardens you'd hear the harness. You'll learn the sounds."
"That's us. The next pair's coming up. Go and get your head down, Caddow."

cartOrders.text: "A Guild cart goes down the Millbridge road tonight, through Hob's Bend, with eight children in it bound for the Sallow hatchery."
"One cart warden. The Guild says a cart of children isn't worth two men's wages. That's their mistake."
"It's your section's job. Brannoc leads. Caddow, you go first to the cart, because the children will trust a woman from the highlands before they trust any of us."

walkBack.text: They walk the children back to the camp through the night. Brannoc carries two of them. Tamsin carries one and sings to her, badly.

quietTamsin.text: Tamsin is on the hay bales, mending a sling, with her boots off and her feet in the last of the sun.
"Sit. You've been walking round this camp like you're looking for something you dropped."

quietTamsin.choose: Tamsin moves up to make room.

options.label: "I keep thinking I'll see Finch in every cart."

do.text: "You will, one day. And it'll be him. And he'll be older, and different, and you'll have to get to know him again. Start getting ready for that now."
"So do I. I ran the cloud path with him a hundred times. I'd have trusted him with my life."
"I did, actually. That's the part I can't get past."

quietTamsin.text: "My mother wore lulls for nine years. I used to count her rings when she was asleep. I don't want to be a person who counts rings any more. So I came up the mountain, and then I came here."
"Whatever you're carrying, Rhea, put some of it down. You can pick it back up. It'll still be there."

quietTamsin.toast: Kane will send for you when there's work.

quietSela.text: Sela is in the kith pens, sitting cross-legged in the straw with a loftbuck foal asleep across her knees.
"Did you know they dream? Their feet go like this. This one's running somewhere."
"At the sorting house they said I'd go to the brood rooms when I was ten. I'm nine now. Nearly."
"I know. I just like to say it, so I remember."

quietOren.text: Oren Tull has come up from Millbridge with a cart of cut stone and a mason's hammer, and is building the nurses a wall that keeps the wind out.
"Anna would have hated this place. Too much mud. She'd have stayed anyway, mind. She stayed with me."
"You told the square the truth when it would have been easy not to. I've thought about that a lot. So here I am."

sallowOrders.text: Kane has a map spread on a crate, held down with stones.
"The Sallow hatchery. Two hundred children, give or take. The Guild has pulled half its Wardens north for the harvest tolls. It won't be this thin again."
"Every section goes. Brannoc's takes the gate. Get your people together, Caddow."

brannocDown.text: Brannoc is lying on his front in the nurses' tent, with his back wrapped in wet linen from shoulders to waist. He turns his head when he hears you.
"Don't. I know what it looks like. The nurse says a month on my belly, and I'm not to laugh, which is no hardship."
"The section needs someone while I'm here. I've told Kane I want it to be you."

options.label: "I've been here four months. They've been here years."

do.text: "And in four months you've stitched half of them and sung the other half to sleep. They know you. That's what it is."
"Not so fast."

brannocDown.text: "It's not mine to give, Caddow. It's not Kane's either. In the Commons, the section chooses. They'll vote at the fire tonight."

sectionVote.text: The section sits round the fire with their bowls. Kane stands at the edge of the light and says nothing at all. This isn't his.
"Brannoc's put Caddow's name up. Anyone else want it?"
Nobody moves. Then Tamsin puts her hand up, and for a moment you think she's standing against you.

"I'll say it, since nobody else will. She's from Larkfold, and Larkfold's greenlings killed people in Millbridge. Some of you lost family to them. If that sticks in your throat, say so now, not later."

then.text: "She stood in the square and owned it, when lying would have won the town quicker. I was there."

else.text: "She told Millbridge the Guild did it. Maybe it did. I'd rather hear her say she doesn't know."

then.text: "She sang my reedcat out of a tree. Then she sat a cold watch with me and listened to me talk rubbish for six hours. I'm for her."
That's all Ketti says. It seems to be enough.

sectionVote.text: The hands go up round the fire, one after another. Not all of them. Enough.
"That's the section's answer, then. Sergeant Caddow."

sectionVote.toast: Promoted: Sergeant. Your section voted for you.

sectionVote.text: "Sergeant Caddow. Go to bed before they make you give a speech."

sparDawn.text: Brannoc is waiting in the drill yard with two practice staves and no expression at all.
"Watch my shoulders, not my hands. When the ring closes, that's when you move. Hit when I'm open. Brace when I'm not."

win.text: "I've set a lot of bones. You learn where people break."
"Don't say that in front of the recruits."
"Right. Three weeks of drill, latrines, cold porridge and the drove road with a sack of stones on your back. Then you can stand a night watch. Go and get your breakfast, Caddow."

then.text: Brannoc's chalked the watch list on a board outside your tent: east picket tonight, Caddow and Ferris.

then.fade: The rains come. A month of quiet at the camp.
Autumn. The first harvest since the raid.

then.text: There's a note pinned to the tent pole, in Tamsin's square hand: "It's harvest. You'll want to go up to Larkfold alone. We'll be here when you come down."

else.toast: Your tent. It's not time to sleep yet.
